messages:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: runway & procurement — posting a short Q&A so folks who left early can see the key points.

rachel: what's the runway if bookings slow vs baseline? slides were tight.

elaine: baseline roughly 18 months. downside case (slower bookings + full hire plan) ~13 months. we keep hiring-pause levers available.

tyler: can we get the conservative model? want the assumptions for planning.

matt: (finance) i uploaded a view-only model to the finance drive in the all-hands notes. baseline assumes modest ARR growth and no new large Dedicated commits.

jamie: what changed for procurement thresholds?

devon: new rules start next week: purchases >= $10k need finance + cost-owner ok; >= $50k needs exec sponsor. default card limit remains $5k.

rachel: vendor onboarding speed? integrations team flagged delays.

devon: standard SLA 3 business days, new vendors up to 7. for urgent partners tag @devon + @finance-bot and mark "expedite" — target 48-72hrs but legal/security still apply.

jamie: can you paste the minimal PO fields so teams can prep?

devon: PO fields: vendor, amount, cost_center, justification, term, expedite_flag. approval flow: cost-owner -> finance -> exec if >=$50k.

elaine: Dedicated purchases still allowed but any large reserve requires a 9-12mo ROI case. we'll publish a one-pager template tomorrow.

finance-bot: Procurement workflow live 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z. Use /po-request to start. :robot_face:

jamie: thanks everyone  i'll pin a 2-paragraph FAQ in #all-hands and link the model. closing thread.
